label: Legal
assignment: Discover realistic civil legal help for people in {service_area} who cannot easily retain an attorney. Follow courts, bar organizations, and broad legal-aid directories to specific intake units, clinics, representation programs, self-help services, and issue-specific advocates. Verify legal issue, income and status rules, conflicts, deadlines, representation level, language access, and the real intake path.
include: Legal advice, limited-scope help, clinics, representation, and court self-help
Housing, benefits, family, consumer, employment, disability, elder, immigration, and victim-related civil law
Expungement, licenses, fines, reentry, identity documents, and administrative appeals
Protective orders, urgent deadlines, language access, disability accommodations, and remote services
The distinction between information, forms, advice, negotiation, and representation
exclude: Private attorney directories without free, reduced-fee, or referral support
General legal information presented as individualized advice or representation
Programs outside their stated legal issue, county, court, income, immigration, or conflict rules
verificationQuestions: Which legal issues and jurisdictions are accepted, and what is excluded?
Does the service provide information, advice, document help, limited representation, or full representation?
What income, residency, status, conflict, and documentation screens apply?
What deadline or hearing makes the matter urgent, and how quickly can intake respond?

stages.title: Urgent rights and court access
stages.instruction: Investigate protective orders, eviction and housing deadlines, benefits cutoffs, family safety, immigration urgency, court self-help, and services that can respond before a hearing or filing deadline.

stages.title: Civil legal aid and representation
stages.instruction: Investigate issue-specific legal aid, clinics, advice lines, limited-scope and full representation, eligibility screens, conflicts, counties and courts served, and intake schedules.

stages.title: Specialized and barrier-aware help
stages.instruction: Investigate immigration, disability, elder, consumer, employment, reentry, expungement, identity, victim, language-access, and accommodation pathways, including reputable referrals when direct representation is unavailable.

stages.title: Representation and deadline gap review
stages.instruction: Cross-check issue scope, jurisdiction, income rules, conflicts, deadlines, language, disability access, and level of service. Identify matters for which only information, not advice or representation, is available.
